title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a directory deactivation removes the user's local password; a re-activation restores access through SSO only
body:
Fixes #32115

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches the SCIM deactivation lifecycle; `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` gains the rule in this change.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：SCIM 目录停用(`active: false`)、删除(`DELETE /Users/{id}`)、让用户失去最后一个活跃来源的连接退役，以及目录把用户保持为停用时的任何后续写入，在 main 已有的封禁、吊销 API key、暂停 AI 服务账号、结束其注册的 OAuth 应用与 SCIM 凭证之外，现在还删除该用户的本地密码(`sys_account` 中 `provider_id = 'credential'` 的行),之后该用户读作目录托管(`idp_provisioned`)。目录重新启用(`active: true` 解除目录自己的封禁)时先删除用户此刻持有的本地密码再解封，访问只经 SSO 恢复；删除未完成则重新启用失败，用户保持停用。
- 为什么改：在案裁决(#32004 评论 6787890900,「Directory deactivation」条)写明「移除目录用户的本地密码是后一步」;API key 一半(#33075)、AI 服务账号(#33109)与注册结束(#36163)已在 main 上，本 PR 合入 main 之后只剩本地密码这一半。维护者 11-17 的「这个不用处理」只免去回填扫尾，修复本身仍欠。
- 风险与回滚：收窄(BREAKING,标题带 `!`):被目录停用过的用户重新启用后没有本地密码，需要时要在重新启用之后有意设置。不做迁移或回填。管理员封禁/解封、管理员封禁之上的 `active: true`、未被封禁用户的目录同步、末位管理员被拒的停用都不删密码。回滚 = 回退本 PR;已删除的密码行不会随回滚恢复。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` 的 `reconcileScimUserLifecycle`(本轮合并解决处：停用分支里 main 的注册结束之后、目录标记之前删除；重新启用分支 fail-closed);`scim-deactivation-password-removal.ts`;`scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts` 的 (l) describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts`,预期 60/60 通过(main 的 45 条 + 本 PR 的 15 条 (l) 用例)。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地(收窄所需的 L2 契约复审由席位路由)。

## What changes

- **The rule.** A directory deactivation removes the user's local password; a re-activation by the directory restores access through SSO only.
  - On every inactive call of `AuthManager#reconcileScimUserLifecycle`, after what `main` already does there (the ban write, the API key revocation, the AI service account suspension, and the ending of the user's OAuth applications and SCIM credentials), and before the directory-managed mark, every `sys_account` row of the user with `provider_id = 'credential'` is deleted. The inactive calls are PATCH `active: false`, `DELETE /Users/{id}`, a create with `active: false`, a tombstone re-link that arrives inactive, a connection decommission pass that removes the user's last active source, and any later SCIM write while the directory holds the user inactive. The trigger is the directory's state, never the ban column.
  - On the `active: true` call that lifts the directory's own ban (`SCIM_DEACTIVATION_BAN_REASON`), the same writer removes any such row the user holds at that moment, inside the same SCIM transaction, before the directory-managed mark and before the unban. A re-activation after a directory deactivation therefore restores no credential from before it, a password an administrator set while the directory held the user deactivated included.
  - The user row, the user's other account links (SSO / OAuth) and the history that names the user are kept (ADR-0134 D3).
- **Writer** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-deactivation-password-removal.ts` (package-internal): reads the row ids only and deletes them through the engine in the system context, attributed to the SCIM connection as a service principal (`authSystemWriteContext`). Idempotent, never throws. `complete` is a measured zero: after deleting, it re-reads and reports `complete` only when no local-password row is left; a row read without an id counts as not removed. At most 100 rows of one user per call, documented in the module header. No audit row follows a delete: `sys_account` is on the audit mirror's skip list.
- **Failure posture, one per branch.** Deactivation: the ban lands first, so an incomplete removal is logged once at `error` and the deprovision still succeeds; the next inactive write runs it again. Re-activation: the ban stays until the removal is complete; an incomplete removal is logged once at `error` and fails the SCIM request, which the vendor rolls back, so the user stays deactivated until the directory retries.
- **Order and the mark.** On a deactivation the removal runs after the ban, so a ban the last-administrator guard refuses throws first and removes nothing. On both branches it runs before the directory-managed mark (ADR-0135 D4), so a user whose password the removal took reads `idp_provisioned`.
- **Sessions.** Unchanged: the vendor deletes the user's sessions after the callback for an inactive state.
- **Unchanged, each pinned by a control:** an administrator's ban and unban; an `active: true` over an administrator's ban; an attribute sync or `active: true` for a user who is not banned; a user with no local password.
- **The directory's ban reason.** A ban whose reason reads `Deactivated via SCIM` is the directory's whoever wrote it: the directory's next active write lifts it and removes the local password (docblock, changeset, docs). Reserving that string on the administrator's ban mount is not done here (L2 N4, Acceptance notes).
- **Docs:** a bullet in `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`, after `main`'s registration-ending bullet: the removal, the decommission door, the `idp_provisioned` mark, the re-activation half, and that no migration or backfill runs. `scim-identity-source.ts`'s header says what the mark reads after the removal.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/32115-directory-deactivation-local-password.md`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch, BREAKING, ADR-0087 disposition not-required (no-migration-prescription). Its BREAKING paragraph now lists the registration ending `main` gained beside the ban, keys and AI service accounts.
- **Census:** `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts/plugins/plugin-auth.md` regenerated by `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` after the merge (never hand-merged): 111 sites, `main`'s 110 plus the writer's one `delete` of `SystemObjectName.ACCOUNT`.

## Tests

Top-level describe in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts`, through `@better-auth/scim` over a real better-sqlite3 engine: "a directory deactivation removes the user's local password, and a re-activation restores access through SSO only". Its fifteen cases are now face **(l)**: `main` added its own (k) describes (an account disabled by any door keeps nothing running in its name), so the merge keeps `main`'s (k) whole and renames this PR's face; no case changed subject.

- (l) `active: false` removes the local password and keeps every other link; the mark reads `idp_provisioned`; `active: true` lifts the ban and restores no password (sign-in `401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD`); the delete is the SCIM connection's write (`isSystem: true`, actor `svc:scim:okta-14360`, no user credited).
- (l) `DELETE /Users/{id}` removes it the same way; a re-link through the tombstone restores none.
- (l) a repeated inactive write sends no delete.
- (l) a deactivation over an administrator's ban removes the password too and keeps the administrator's reason.
- (l) CONTROL: an administrator's ban and unban leave the password alone.
- (l) CONTROL: an attribute sync or an `active: true` for a user who is not banned removes nothing; only lifting the directory's ban does (positive leg: one delete).
- (l) a re-activation after a directory deactivation restores no credential from before it, the deactivated state seeded directly; attribution asserted.
- (l) CONTROL: `active: true` over an administrator's ban lifts nothing and removes nothing.
- (l) CONTROL: a user with no local password is a no-op.
- (l) a refused deactivation of the last administrator (PATCH and DELETE) attempts no delete.
- (l) a deactivation that fails after the removal rolls the removal back with the ban.
- (l) a removal that cannot be written on a deactivation still bans, logs once at `error`, and the next inactive write removes it.
- (l) a removal that cannot be written on a re-activation fails it (status ≥ 500), logs once, and keeps the user deactivated; the retry re-activates with no password.
- (l) a removal is complete only when a re-read finds no local password.
- (l) a local-password row read without an id counts as not removed.

Cases changed because the behaviour changed (unchanged from the earlier rounds): "(b) active:true ⇒ the SCIM ban is lifted, and the re-activation restores no local password from before it", and the faces (a), (d), (f) and the cause cases, which set the password again after the deactivation before signing in.

## Acceptance notes

- Premise re-measured on `origin/main` `f46ce5b4af`: the API-key half (#33075, `revokeDirectoryDeactivatedApiKeys`), the AI service account suspension (#33109) and the registration ending (#36163, `endScimDeactivatedRegistrations`) are on `main`; the inactive branch deletes no `credential` row and the active branch only unbans. Only the local-password half still reproduces, and it is this PR's whole delta against `main` (7 paths, +1027 / −26).
- Merge of `origin/main` `f46ce5b4af` (merge commit `c7c85d60c3`, no rebase, no force push): four files conflicted. `auth-manager.ts` keeps `main`'s registration ending and runs the removal after it, before the mark; the test file keeps `main`'s new describes whole and renames this PR's face to (l); `authentication.mdx` keeps both bullets; the census shard was taken from `main` and regenerated (`f635db10e8`).
- The maintainer's 「这个不用处理」 (11-17) waives only the residual backfill sweep. No migration or backfill runs: a user deactivated before this version keeps their local credential until the directory next writes that user. An administrator's unban removes nothing.
- Seat answers on the round-0 questions (delta r1): the removal runs on every inactive write, a connection decommission pass included; the last-local-credential guard stays off on the SCIM path; the break-glass last-administrator guard still refuses first.
- L2 nits (record 6946949332, at `1540d3a270`): N1, N2, N3 and N5 applied in round 3; N4 documented, not reserved (reserving the string adds a refusal to the administrator's ban door, outside this card); N6 and S1 belong to the ADR bookkeeping card.
- ADR bookkeeping: #34820
- The connection decommission door is named from the vendor's code path (`reconcileSCIMProjectionDomainBatch` calls `identity.reconcileUser`), not driven by a case in this file.
- Records on file are at `1540d3a270` (L1 ACCEPT 6946960271, L2 PASS 6946949332) and do not cover this head; the round-3 delta and this merge are unreviewed.
- `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts` now runs 60 cases (45 on `main`). Budget line `test-budget: 20` stands, re-measured LOCALLY at 60 cases (10.52 s, the slowest of four runs of the file alone, × 1.25); the line says the reading is local.
